column1: # testing/fleet-fixtures/service-images.tsv — THE pinned service-image list for the durable-store QA
# cycle. See docs/design/store-qa-cycle.md.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The provisioning of the four backend services the store plugins need was
# written FIVE times — .github/workflows/ci.yml's `check` and `coverage` jobs, release-stage.yml's
# `gate` job, plugin-ci.yml's `build-test-signoff` job, and scripts/release-check.sh. The four
# workflows agreed on a digest; release-check.sh — the script the QA GATE runs — used FLOATING tags
# (`postgres:16`, `mysql:8`, `valkey/valkey:8`, `hashicorp/vault`), so the qa gate was not pinned to
# the bytes CI was pinned to. Five sources of truth agree until the day one of them is edited.
# So: ONE pinned file, everything reads it — the same shape testing/shadow-oracle/golden-digests.tsv
# and plugin-digests.tsv already use for release artifacts and plugin tarballs, for the same reason.
# GitHub Actions cannot read a file into a `services:` block, so the workflows keep literal `image:`
# lines and scripts/service-images-check.sh asserts every one of them matches a row here. A digest
# bump then lands in one commit and the lint proves the fan-out was complete.
# RE-PINNING. `docker buildx imagetools inspect <tag>` (ci.yml, release-stage.yml both do this
# already). The natural home for the periodic bump is .github/workflows/monthly-refresh.yml.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; `#` comments and blank lines ignored)
#   service      the name plugins.yaml uses in its `service:` field, and the name
#                testing/fleet-fixtures/store-services.sh takes as its argument
#   image        the image REFERENCE as it appears in a workflow's `image:` line, without the digest
#   digest       sha256:… — the pin. A workflow `image:` line must read exactly `<image>@<digest>`
#   ready_probe  the command run INSIDE the container to prove readiness, or `-` when the service
#                has no local runner here. Readiness is PROVEN, never slept on
#                (polling decides whether the test can BEGIN,
#                never whether it passed)
#   port         the port the service listens on inside the container
#   local_port   the host port store-services.sh publishes it on, DELIBERATELY OFFSET from the
#                default so a developer's own postgres on 5432 is never touched, and equally
#                deliberately nowhere near the shadow oracle's own 487xx/488xx band. `-` = no local
#                runner. These are exactly the offsets scripts/release-check.sh already uses.
#   ready_secs   the cap on the readiness poll, in seconds. mysql's is 120 and not 60 because
#                MySQL 8's FIRST boot initialises the datadir and restarts once; measured in
#                release-check.sh. Exceeding a cap is a RED naming the service, never a retry.
# service
postgres
mysql
valkey
vault
wiremock
